newsitem.title: USA: USDA PROPOSES SHORTER HORSE QUARANTINE FROM MEXICO.
newsitem.headline: USDA PROPOSES SHORTER HORSE QUARANTINE FROM MEXICO.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Thursday it was proposing to end a requirement that horses from Mexico be quarantined for seven days before entering the United States.

The seven-day quarantine was imposed last summer after Mexican authorities reported that Venezuelan equine encephalomyelitis had been detected in Mexico. The disease is transmitted mainly by mosquitos and other blood-feeding insects and has a high mortality rate.
No case of the disease has been reported in the past 12 months in Mexico, USDA said, so ending the seven-day quarantine would not pose a risk to U.S. horses.
Horses imported from Mexico would continue to be held in quarantine,usually for three or four days, until it was determined they were free of exotic pests and diseases.
